case_facts: My employer terminated me without notice or severance after I reported unsafe working conditions; I had a 4-year permanent contract.

analysis.summary: A permanently employed worker with a 4-year contract was summarily terminated without notice or severance pay after reporting unsafe working conditions to their employer. The termination appears to be retaliatory in nature, raising issues of wrongful dismissal, whistleblower protection, and statutory entitlements under Indian labour law. The employee seeks remedies including reinstatement, back wages, and compensation.

issues.issue: Wrongful termination without notice or severance in violation of statutory retrenchment norms
Retaliatory dismissal / victimisation for reporting unsafe working conditions amounting to unfair labour practice
issues.governing_law: Fifth Schedule, Industrial Disputes Act 1947; Whistleblower Protection Act 2014

issues.issue: Employer's duty to maintain safe working conditions and non-penalisation of employees who report hazards
issues.governing_law: Sections 7A, 7B, Factories Act 1948; Occupational Safety Health and Working Conditions Code 2020

issues.issue: Entitlement to reinstatement with full back wages and continuity of service for a permanent contract employee

governing_acts: Section 2(s) Industrial Disputes Act workman definition

retaliatory dismissal victimisation unsafe working conditions whistleblower

plan.esql: FROM legal-judgments | WHERE (text LIKE '*wrongful termination*' OR text LIKE '*retaliatory dismissal*' OR text LIKE '*victimisation*' OR text LIKE '*retrenchment*' OR text LIKE '*unsafe working conditions*') AND (text LIKE '*Industrial Disputes Act*' OR text LIKE '*Section 25F*' OR text LIKE '*Factories Act*' OR text LIKE '*Whistleblower*') | KEEP title, headline, catchwords, text, date | LIMIT 10
plan.search_rationale: The DSL bool/should query blends multi_match across all key text fields for the core fact patterns (retaliatory dismissal, unsafe conditions, reinstatement) with targeted term boosts on the most directly applicable statutory entities (Section 25F, Industrial Disputes Act 1947, Factories Act 1948, Whistleblower Protection Act), ensuring both factually similar cases and on-point statutory precedents are surfaced. The ES|QL statement provides a complementary keyword filter sweep across the full-text and metadata fields to catch any judgments not scored highly by relevance ranking.
